title: "Fate Chess Game"
next_chapter_hook: "Deep within the mural, a pair of eyes silent for ten thousand years slowly opened, gazing upon all this..."

text.content: "At the end of the dim corridor, a phosphorescent glow seeped through the stone wall cracks, casting Chen Ji's face in alternating light and shadow. He stood with hands clasped behind his back before a broken stone tablet, his gaze fixed死死 on the sacrificial mural that had just revealed its full appearance, his spine rigid as iron. The pupils that had moments ago carried a hint of inquiry were now being devoured, inch by inch, by something far more abyssal—there was fury, yet it was more than fury. Beside him, Su Qingyao stood askance, her fingertips quietly resting on her sword hilt, brow furrowed. She recognized this look on Chen Ji. In three years, this was the first time she had seen him wear his emotions so undisguised on his face. A foreboding premonition arose unbidden in her heart."

"The mural consisted of nine panels, layered upon each other like a history sealed within stone. The first panel: across the vast land, a dozen figures stood facing the sky, each with a faint glow flickering at their brow center—that was the Tianji Record in its original form of bestowal. The second panel: the dozen individuals fought separately, using their foresight to stir the winds and clouds, once hailed as a divine miracle. But by the third panel, the scene shifted abruptly: the heavens and earth shattered, the sky dyed in blood, countless cities turned to scorched earth, and upon that scorched earth, the original seers knelt one by one, the light at their brow centers forcibly extracted by a colossal eye descending from the heavens, injected into a key as black as ink."

""Is this... the Ancient Great Cataclysm?" Su Qingyao lowered her voice, unconsciously stepping half a pace closer to Chen Ji. Chen Ji did not answer. His gaze was locked死死 on the fourth panel—beneath that obsidian key, a dozen skeletons formed a诡异的 circle, and at the circle's center, a blurry figure held the key in both hands, their expression a blend of relief and despair that defied description. Below the mural, an ancient seal script was carved. Chen Ji deciphered each character one by one, his pupils contracting sharply: "The Tianji Record is not a vessel of bestowed destiny, but a lock of sealing. Each record-keeper serves as kindling for the cataclysm.""

dialogue.content: "（Cold laugh）Kindling... so that's it. Ten thousand years of inheritance, merely burning one batch of firewood after another."

text.content: "Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm, like the icy waters of a frozen abyss stripped of all warmth. He walked slowly toward the fifth panel, fingertips touching the cold stone surface, as if trying to reach through the faded pigments to grasp the truth of ten thousand years ago. In the fifth painting, the figure holding the key had vanished, replaced by a massive altar. Upon the altar, a new inheritor was bound to a pillar, the faint light at their brow center rekindled—the Tianji Record was being passed on. However, this time, sprawled beneath the inheritor's feet lay a corpse, its face identical to the previous record-keeper. The price of inheritance was never any heavenly mandate—it was stepping over the predecessor's bones to advance."

"Su Qingyao's breath caught abruptly. She turned sharply to look at Chen Ji's profile, seeing his jawline taut as a bowstring, his Adam's apple subtly bobbing, yet he remained silent. She had never seen him like this—that man who always had things under control, who manipulated everything with effortless skill, now seemed as if someone had brutally snapped his spine. "Chen Ji..." she spoke, her voice carrying a rare tremor she herself had not noticed, "the murals may not all be true. Ancient secrets are difficult to verify—""

"Chen Ji suddenly raised his hand, cutting her off. He pointed to the sixth panel, his voice hoarse as grinding stone: "Senior Sister Su, look here." Su Qingyao gazed intently—the sixth painting depicted the altar transformed into a sect, a plaque hanging above the sect, its characters blurred beyond recognition, but the architectural style was unmistakably the Tianqing Sect! And within the sect's great hall, a man dressed in Tianqing robes knelt on the ground, hands holding the fragmented Tianji Record, his face contorted as if enduring tremendous agony. Above his head, a colossal eye extended from the clouds, coldly overlooking all."

"Chen Ji suddenly let out a low laugh. That laughter echoed through the dim corridor, making Su Qingyao's scalp tingle. "I have been wondering," his voice light as a whisper, "whether the Tianji Record chose me out of pity for this废物, or with some ulterior design. Now it seems—" he turned sharply, an unfamiliar light burning in his pupils that Su Qingyao had never witnessed before, "it wasn't selecting a person at all. It was selecting firewood.""

choice.prompt: "Chen Ji's belief experienced its first fundamental tremor—he must make a choice"

choices.description: "Even if the truth is more cruel, he must see the full picture of this ten-thousand-year chess game. Truth matters more than comfort."

text.content: "Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the surging tide of rage in his heart, and turned toward the seventh panel. His fingers trembled slightly, yet he forced himself forward step by step. Su Qingyao wanted to pull him back, but was stopped by a single look from him—that gaze held a resolve she had never witnessed before."

choices.description: "The aura emanating from the murals grows increasingly strange; do not act rashly. Impulsiveness may trigger unknown traps."
choices.process_label: 恢复冷静，伸手阻止苏青瑶

text.content: "Chen Ji suddenly whipped around, seizing Su Qingyao's wrist and pulling her behind him. His movement was crisp and decisive, not even glancing back at her: "Don't touch. The aura on these murals is wrong." Su Qingyao froze—he had been on the edge of emotional breakdown moments ago, yet now had recovered that chilling composure."

"The instant the seventh panel came into Chen Ji's view, the blood in his entire body seemed to freeze simultaneously. In the painting, a man in black robes stood before the Tianji Record Fragment. His features were deliberately blurred, but beside him stood a figure Chen Ji knew intimately—Old Sect Master Ling Yuan! The black-robed man extended his hand, passing a page of the fragmented Tianji Record to Ling Yuan, while at Ling Yuan's feet lay a corpse lying face-up, a dagger thrust into its chest, its face smeared with blood and unidentifiable. But the robe style on that corpse was identical to the Tianqing Sect Servant Robe Chen Ji wore."

dialogue.content: "（Inhaling sharply）This... the person in this painting, is it Sect Master Ling? And that corpse at his feet... Chen Ji, is that... you...?"

text.content: "Chen Ji did not answer. In his mind, fragments were being pieced together at an suffocating speed—Old Sect Master Ling Yuan, the previous candidate for the Tianji Record, the one 'skipped' by the Tianji Record. The blurred corpse in the mural, the transmission of the Tianji Record, and his own bizarre experience of inexplicably becoming the new record-keeper... every thread pointed toward a possibility that made his spine crawl: he had not been chosen by the Tianji Record, but 'manufactured' by Ling Yuan. Those adventures he thought were his own, those arrangements he believed were heaven's design—all were a meticulously crafted script."

"Chen Ji's fists slowly clenched tight, his knuckles blanching. A primitive, scalding fury rose from the depths of his chest, threatening to incinerate his rationality. Ten thousand years. For ten thousand years he had thought he was playing a grand chess game of heaven-shaking magnitude, never knowing he was merely the most insignificant piece on the board—one cultivated with care, awaiting combustion. His schemes, his patience, all the humiliations he endured—everything became a joke in this moment. But he did not let the fury consume him. Three breaths later, he inhaled deeply, the madness in his eyes forcibly suppressed, replaced by something far more terrifying—calm. He noted it. He told himself. This debt, he noted it. Ling Yuan, the Eye of Heavenly Dao, and those so-called manipulators of destiny—he would not let a single one escape."

"Su Qingyao watched Chen Ji collapse and reconstruct himself within mere moments, her heart feeling as if someone had violently twisted it. She suddenly recalled the scene when she first noticed this servant disciple three years ago—at that time, she had only thought him dull and useless. Now she realized, every time he yielded before her, it was merely an act. And now, this man stood atop the ruins of ten-thousand-year truth, rebuilding his worldview in a near-cruel manner. No one knew how much pain he carried. Because nothing showed on his face."

"The eighth panel's light illuminated Chen Ji's eyes. In this painting, the Tianji Record had fully transformed into a golden tome, and beneath the golden tome赫然 was a massive chessboard. Upon the chessboard, countless points of light sparkled like stars—each point was a destiny trajectory of a Tianji Record user. Without exception, all were converging toward a巨大的 vortex at the board's center. And at the vortex's center, four characters were written: Heavenly Mandate Unifies. Chen Ji stared at those four characters, and suddenly understood. Heavenly Mandate Unification meant rekindling the extinguished fire of the Heavenly Dao using countless seers' heavenly fate as fuel. And he was merely another piece of firewood about to be cast into the flames."

choice.prompt: "The ultimate truth revealed by the murals forces Chen Ji to choose—accept destiny or shatter the chessboard"

choices.description: "If Heaven wants to burn me, I shall burn Heaven first. Even if shattered into pieces, I will tear apart this veil of fate."
choices.visible_cost: "Risk of angering the Heavenly Mandate's will"
choices.visible_reward: "First step in breaking free from destiny"
choices.risk_hint: "Opposing Heaven's Mandate alone is like an egg striking a rock"
choices.process_label: 将怒火化为破坏棋局的决心

dialogue.content: "（Suddenly raising his palm, gathering a blinding spiritual light）Since we are all firewood, let's make this fire burn more brilliantly. Heaven wants to burn me?—Then let it taste the flavor of backlash first!"

text.content: "Su Qingyao had never witnessed Chen Ji so undisguised. He was always the chess master pulling strings from the shadows, capable of maintaining composure even when Mount Tai was collapsing. But at this moment, spiritual energy churned around him, the stone tiles beneath his feet beginning to crack, a savage aura gushed from within him like a tangible wave—the most primal, instinctive roar after ten thousand years of being deceived by destiny."

choices.description: "Anger solves nothing. He needs more truth, a larger chess game, to drag the manipulators off their divine pedestals."
choices.visible_reward: "Gain a more complete understanding of the chess game"
choices.risk_hint: "May be seen as weakness or capitulation"
choices.process_label: 强行压下怒火，恢复冷静分析

dialogue.content: "（Slowly收敛breath, voice low as an abyss）...No. Not yet. Ten thousand years of布局, someone must be more impatient than me."

text.content: "Su Qingyao watched silently as he retracted the savage aura into his body piece by piece, an indescribable bitterness welling in her heart. She suddenly realized, the weight this man carried was far heavier than she could fathom. She said nothing, merely stepping forward one pace to stand at his side. Words were unnecessary. She was telling him in her own way—you are not alone."

"Chen Ji withdrew the spiritual light in his palm and turned toward the final panel—the ninth mural. The instant his gaze touched it, he froze completely. In the ninth painting, a figure stood with back to all beings, black hair cascading down, form identical to Chen Ji—it was Chen Xuan. Chen Xuan from ten thousand years ago. But what was bizarre: Chen Xuan was not alone. Before him, a blurred outline faced him in confrontation. The outline had no face, only one eye—a cold, supreme, Heavenly Dao's Eye overlooking all beings. And Chen Xuan's lips were moving, seemingly speaking to that eye. In the corner of the painting, in a color like blood, a line was inscribed: Chen Xuan attempted to break this cycle. But ultimately, he chose another way."

"Chen Ji's gaze locked on that line, his fingertips trembling involuntarily. Chen Xuan chose another way? What way? Passing truth to later generations, or—He suddenly recalled the voice within the first page of the Tianji Record, the one that had been guarding him as a remnant soul. Mo Xiansheng. Each volume of objectives completed allowed one page of knowledge to be unsealed. In other words, Chen Xuan split the method of breaking the cycle into countless fragments, hiding them within the Tianji Record. He did not directly tell Chen Ji the answer, but used a crueler method—making Chen Ji find it himself, choose for himself. Had Chen Xuan ten thousand years ago also stood before this same mural, experiencing the same despair and rage? And what was the "another way" he ultimately chose?"

"Just then, the phosphorescent light of the murals suddenly shuddered violently. That Heavenly Dao's Eye that had been faintly visible deep within the mural actually slowly opened its pupil within the ninth panel—a gaze cold to the extreme, staring at Chen Ji from within the stone wall. That gaze held no hostility, no warmth, only a... scrutiny transcending all emotion. As if saying: So now you know. Then, that eye slowly closed, the mural returned to darkness, and only Chen Ji's heavy breathing and the whitened knuckles of Su Qingyao gripping her sword hilt remained in the corridor."

"After a long while, Chen Ji spoke. His voice had regained its usual composure, but the undercurrents churning beneath that calm, anyone could perceive clearly. "Senior Sister Su." He turned his head, looking at this woman who had been silently keeping watch beside him, the corner of his lips lifting in an extremely faint arc, "What do you think a person should do after discovering they have been a chess piece from the very beginning?" Su Qingyao met his gaze, seeing what burned in the depths of those pupils—not despair, not rage, but something far more terrifying than either. That was resolve. That was the determination of a chess master toyed with by destiny for ten thousand years, to overturn the entire board. "I don't know." she said frankly, releasing her sword hilt and grasping his wrist instead, "But whatever you do, I am here."
